issues.label: Supply Chain Collapse
issues.summary: Cascading failures across interconnected logistics systems — production halted, shelves empty, critical goods unavailable

circuits.detail: Supply chain orchestration overwhelmed — too many simultaneous disruptions for executive planning to manage
Inventory management systems in crisis mode — safety stocks depleted, reorder signals firing continuously
Warehouse inventories critically low — buffer stock exhausted, no replacement shipments in pipeline
Trucking networks paralyzed by driver shortages, fuel costs, and regulatory bottlenecks
Logistics technology systems generating alerts faster than human operators can process and act
Last-mile delivery failing — parcels delayed, customer satisfaction collapsing, returns spiking

issues.label: Port Blockade
issues.summary: Major port operations halted by congestion, labor action, geopolitical closure, or infrastructure failure

circuits.detail: Port terminals gridlocked — vessel queue extending to weeks, container dwell times tripling
Shipping routes diverted to secondary ports — transit times increasing, costs spiraling
Warehouses near blocked ports overflowing while inland facilities sit empty — spatial mismatch
Rail connections to blocked ports severed — intermodal scheduling cascading into failures
Inventory systems unable to track goods stranded in transit — visibility lost across blocked corridors

issues.label: Trade War
issues.summary: Retaliatory tariffs, sanctions, and trade restrictions disrupting established commercial relationships

circuits.detail: Tariff schedules changing unpredictably — customs costs doubling overnight, landed cost calculations invalidated
Trade agreements under strain or abrogated — decades of diplomatic relationship-building eroding
Commodity prices crashing in sanctioned markets while spiking in non-sanctioned alternatives
Supply chain strategies invalidated — sourcing decisions based on now-banned trade relationships
Cross-border commercial trust collapsing — counterparties unwilling to enter long-term contracts
Rail freight corridors through sanctioned territories disrupted — land bridge routes compromised

issues.label: Shipping Crisis
issues.summary: Maritime disruption from piracy, canal closure, extreme weather, or vessel shortage causing global freight emergency

circuits.detail: Major shipping lanes compromised — Suez, Panama, or Strait of Malacca closures forcing circumnavigation
Air freight demand surging as maritime alternative — cargo rates spiking 3-5x, capacity rationed
Port schedules shattered — vessels arriving out of sequence, berth allocation chaotic
Cold chain integrity threatened — temperature-sensitive cargo stranded on diverted vessels exceeding transit time limits
Supply chain managers scrambling to reroute, rebook, and re-source across all affected trade lanes simultaneously

issues.label: Customs Disruption
issues.summary: Border processing failures from regulatory changes, system outages, or inspection backlogs halting cross-border flow

circuits.detail: New regulatory requirements imposed without transition period — compliance impossible for goods already in transit
Cross-border mutual recognition suspended — every shipment requiring full inspection and documentation review
Freight forwarders unable to bridge regulatory gap — documentation rejected at multiple borders simultaneously
Trucks queuing at borders for days — driver hours expiring, perishable cargo spoiling, costs mounting
Trade agreement frameworks failing to prevent unilateral customs policy changes — diplomatic channels ineffective
Inventory management blinded — goods stuck in customs with no estimated release date, reorder calculations impossible
